transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess I came in because I’ve been having a really hard time sitting still. Like in the radiology suite or in class, when I’m supposed to just stay put, I start feeling really restless—almost like I’m crawling out of my skin.

I tried to just deal with it for a while, because I know everyone gets antsy sometimes, but it’s been months and I still end up pacing, shifting around, or kind of looking for an excuse to get up and move. I don’t know if that makes sense, but it’s been getting hard to manage.
Does this restlessness happen in other places too, like at home or with friends, or is it mostly when you’re in class or at work?

It’s mostly when I’m expected to sit still, like in the radiology suite or in class. I mean, I guess it can feel like it’s just… me being antsy, but it gets pretty uncomfortable, like crawling out of my skin.

I try not to make it a big deal, but after a while I end up shifting around, pacing if I can, or looking for some reason to get up and move. Does that answer what you mean?
